transcript.user_1_turn_1: I'm making a little label for my homemade cookie jar, and somehow three short phrases are taking up my whole brain.
transcript.user_2_turn_1: A cookie jar deserves unreasonable levels of editorial attention. What are the finalists?
transcript.user_1_turn_2: Cookies: take one, smile twice. Tiny Treats Inside. And Emergency Cookies — For Crumbly Days.
transcript.user_2_turn_2: The first is warm and clear, the second is the shortest, and the third is definitely the joke option.
transcript.user_1_turn_3: The jar is squat glass with a pretty small cream label, and kids will be reading it too.
transcript.user_2_turn_3: Then readability matters more than squeezing in the cleverest line.
transcript.user_1_turn_4: That's why Tiny Treats worries me a little. It could be dog biscuits or candy or anything.
transcript.user_2_turn_4: Yeah, if you want instant recognition, actually saying 'cookies' does useful work.
transcript.user_1_turn_5: I still want it to feel friendly, though. Not like I printed COOKIE INVENTORY on the side of the jar.
transcript.user_2_turn_5: Clear doesn't have to mean sterile. A short warm phrase can still be easy to read.
transcript.user_1_turn_6: I keep coming back to the first one because it actually says cookies and still sounds welcoming. I just don't want the little label to feel crowded.
